Description: A logo consisting entirely of a stylized company name set in a custom or chosen typeface.
Construction: Custom letterforms on a baseline grid; tight tracking; optical kerning adjustments
Scalability Note: Readable down to ~16px if typeface is clean; collapses to favicon initial at very small sizes
Vector Requirement: Must be SVG <path> outlines so any renderer can scale without font-dependency or raster blur
Avoid When: Brand name is long or hard to pronounce; international markets require localized scripts

Description: One to three initials treated as a standalone graphic mark, often with custom ligatures.
Construction: Two or three letterforms composed on a shared grid; ligatures optically balanced
Scalability Note: Excellent at small sizes - single glyph reads instantly as favicon or app icon
Vector Requirement: True vector required; raster versions pixelate at retina densities and lose ligature crispness
Avoid When: Company name is already short and memorable enough to stand alone as a wordmark

Description: A recognizable real-world object or icon used as the sole brand identifier, no text.
Industry Fit: Consumer tech; sports; retail; food and beverage
Construction: Simplified silhouette reduced to essential contours; built on a geometric skeleton
Scalability Note: Scales from billboard to 16px favicon cleanly when unnecessary detail is removed at design time
Vector Requirement: SVG <path> is mandatory; any bitmap detail renders as mud at small icon sizes
Avoid When: Brand is unknown - pictorial marks require years of recognition before standing alone

Description: A non-representational geometric form that conveys brand values through shape and color.
Industry Fit: B2B technology; consulting; financial services; biotech
Construction: Constructed from geometric primitives on a strict grid; proportions derived from golden ratio or modular scale
Scalability Note: Highly scalable as it contains no fine detail; works as app icon with no modification
Vector Requirement: Vector <path> essential; abstract marks are precision objects and raster blurs their mathematical edges
Avoid When: Brand needs immediate intuitive communication of a product category to new audiences

Description: A wordmark and symbol presented together as a single lockup with defined clear-space rules.
Industry Fit: Most industry sectors - the most versatile logo format
Construction: Symbol placed left of or above the wordmark; aligned on a shared baseline; proportional size ratio defined in brand guide
Scalability Note: Can separate into symbol-only or wordmark-only responsive variants for small placements
Vector Requirement: Each element must be a separate SVG layer so the lockup can be split for responsive use without raster degradation
Avoid When: Space is extremely constrained and only one mark variant will ever be used

Description: The name and a symbol are enclosed inside a containing shape such as a shield, circle, or crest.
Industry Fit: Breweries; universities; sports teams; heritage brands; automotive
Construction: Outer shape contains arranged type arcs and central device; letterpress-era inspired construction
Scalability Note: Loses fine interior detail below 48px; a simplified badge variant is typically required for favicon use
Vector Requirement: Vector is critical - the interior complexity of badge elements becomes unrecognizable in raster at small sizes
Avoid When: Digital-first products that appear primarily as small icons or in dense UI environments

Description: A character - illustrated figure or creature - that acts as brand spokesperson and logo element.
Industry Fit: Food and beverage; sports; children's brands; gaming; insurance
Construction: Character illustration with defined poses; color palette limited for reproduction consistency; brand guide covers expression library
Scalability Note: Cannot scale to favicon; a separate abstract or initial-based icon is always required alongside it
Vector Requirement: Vector illustration preferred for scalability; raster mascots are acceptable only if minimum-size usage is strictly avoided
Avoid When: B2B enterprise; legal; medical; financial sectors where authority and trust must read instantly

Description: A mark constructed from repeated or interlocking geometric modules - squares; circles; triangles.
Industry Fit: Architecture; engineering; data; fintech; design agencies
Construction: Grid-based modules locked to precise intervals; negative space between modules is part of the design intent
Scalability Note: Scales cleanly because the building blocks are simple; modules may merge into a solid shape at very small sizes
Vector Requirement: SVG paths must encode each module as a closed shape so module colors and spacing remain editable and renderer-agnostic
Avoid When: Brands that need warmth or organic character; hospitality or wellness sectors

Description: A mark where a hidden secondary image is revealed in the space between or within primary shapes.
Industry Fit: Design-forward brands; food; retail; clever challenger brands
Construction: Two overlapping or adjacent positive shapes engineered so the gap forms a recognizable third image
Scalability Note: Can be fragile at small sizes if the negative-space detail disappears; test at 24px before approving
Vector Requirement: Vector mandatory - raster anti-aliasing destroys the sharp edge contrast on which the illusion depends
Avoid When: Audiences who will encounter the mark only at small digital sizes and never in print or large-format

Description: A mark that uses color gradients, shadows, or dimensional rendering to suggest depth or light.
Industry Fit: Consumer apps; entertainment; gaming; lifestyle tech
Construction: Gradient mesh or linear/radial gradient applied over a vector base form; highlight and shadow layers stacked
Scalability Note: Degrades to flat color at small sizes; a flat fallback variant is required in brand guidelines
Vector Requirement: Base shape must be SVG <path>; gradient appearance is a style layer - the structural mark must work without it
Avoid When: Embossing; foil stamping; or single-color print contexts where gradients cannot reproduce

Description: A mark system with defined variants that adapt layout or complexity to available space or context.
Industry Fit: Large digital platforms; media networks; enterprise software suites
Construction: Core symbol plus rules for 3-4 variants ranging from full lockup to icon-only; grid defines reduction breakpoints
Scalability Note: Purpose-built for small sizes - the icon variant is the small-size solution by design
Vector Requirement: Each variant must be a separate SVG file with <path> elements; automated raster export from each variant covers all densities
Avoid When: Small organizations without resources to maintain a multi-variant system consistently

Description: A logotype where the letterforms are uniquely drawn or heavily modified to be a proprietary typeface.
Industry Fit: Premium consumer brands; fashion houses; editorial media; cultural institutions
Construction: Letters drawn from scratch or derived from an existing typeface then heavily modified; each glyph refined for optical balance
Scalability Note: Works at most sizes if letterforms are open and not overly decorative; condensed custom cuts can collapse at favicon scale
Vector Requirement: Outlines must be expanded to SVG <path> curves so the mark is independent of any font file and renders identically everywhere
Avoid When: Brands requiring frequent name updates or localization into non-Latin scripts
